Risk officer view: I would refuse this buy.

Key reasons from the brief:
- Class is labeled ORGANIC, but the curve shows 75% bundle share, a launch bot present, and sell-to-buy of 1.52 in the first two minutes. That is manipulation-shaped, not organic.
- Net outflow of -13.8 SOL over the last 15 minutes, return -33%, and a 40% drawdown from the 30-minute high. Sellers outnumber the buying pressure.
- Pool depth of ~64 SOL is thin. A $20 round trip would pay 1.4-5.1% in fees and impact, and exits in a falling market would be worse.

If the desk overrode this and bought anyway, the cap would be $5, stop at 20%, and a 15-minute hold, since the trend is down and liquidity is shallow. But the default is to skip. A missed coin costs nothing; this one fits the profile of a bad buy.
memos.scout:
The honest case for buying e/world now is weak. Its class label says ORGANIC and it is alive, with 159 buyers, no airdrop dump, and a pool of about 64 SOL. But the brief undercuts most of that. The last 15 minutes show net outflow of -13.84 SOL, with sell volume (26.35 SOL) more than double buy volume (12.51 SOL) and 44 sellers against 45 buyers. Price is down 33% over that window and 38% over 30 minutes, with a 40% drawdown from the 30-minute high. The first two minutes after graduation had a sell-to-buy ratio of 1.52, and the top five buyers took about half of early volume. Bundle share is 75%, which suggests coordinated early buying, and the completer share is 35%.

Nothing in the brief shows demand that is holding up. Sellers are outnumbering buyers in the most recent window, and the pattern looks like a dip that has not found a floor. I see no case that clears the base rate of roughly 20% loss per trade. The desk should skip this coin.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss: insider distribution into a drawdown that never recovers. The curve shows bundle_share 0.75 and completer_share 0.35, so most early supply was bundled and the completer holds a large slice. Post-graduation, sell_to_buy_ratio is 1.52 and top5_buyer_share is 0.50, meaning a handful of early wallets are the main sellers. Last 15 minutes: sell_sol 26.35 against buy_sol 12.51, net_flow -13.84 SOL, return -33%, with 44 sellers outnumbering 45 buyers. The 40% drawdown from the 30-minute high is still open, and the pool is only 63.9 SOL deep, so a $20 buy faces meaningful impact both ways. A 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost on a coin in active distribution leaves no realistic edge. Skip.
